c-di-GMP controls a variety of cellular processes in V. cholcaere, including flagellar biosynthesis, biofilm development and motility.

elucidating the role of c-di-Gmp in V. cholereae.
elucidating the molecular basis of c-di-Gmp mediated gene regulation in V. cholerra.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

V. choleroe responds to an increased level of c-di GMP by decreasing the transcription of flagellar genes and increasing the transcription of genes involved in the production of extracellular structures.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
c-di-GMP controls the transition from a motile to a sessile life style.
c-di-GMP is involved in regulating a number of cellular processes in V. chol erae, including motility, virulence factor production, biofilm formation, and cell envelope integrity.
c-di-GMP regulates the transcription of a number of V. chol erae genes involved in motility, biofilm formation, and cell surface properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
c-di-GMP regulates the expression of many genes in V. cholerae.
V. cholerea is a versatile pathogen that can adapt to a variety of environmental conditions by regulating the expression of genes involved in different processes.
the c-di-GMP level in V. cholereae is an important regulator of the transition from motility to sessility.
